CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right leg pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 43-year-old female presenting with right upper leg pain sustained during a bowling injury. While running up to the lane with a bowling ball, patient accidentally struck her right leg with the ball instead of releasing it down the lane and subsequently fell. She denies significant swelling but reports mild bruising on the posterior/lateral aspect of the leg. Pain is severe with ambulation; patient ambulates only with difficulty and careful movement. She reports she would avoid stairs. Patient has been self-managing pain with alternating doses of ibuprofen and tylenol.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient with known atopic eczema. No other acute symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Atopic eczema
2. Colectomy for diverticulitis

MEDICATIONS
1. Fluocinonide - topical, as needed for eczema
2. Ibuprofen - over-the-counter, as needed
3. Tylenol - over-the-counter, as needed

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is an active bowler.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Significant tenderness to palpation over the lateral aspect of the right upper leg. No pain or tenderness with flexion or extension of the lower leg.

RESULTS
Right femur x-ray: Normal. No evidence of fracture or swelling.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right upper leg contusion. Started on mobic 15 mg orally once daily for anti-inflammatory effect. Patient instructed to use ice for pain management. Expected improvement within one week. Patient to return if symptoms do not improve.
